title: Biobank Lead (Senior Manager / Associate Director)
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Quotient is seeking an experienced, detail-oriented operational leader to run the management, process control, governance and quality leadership of its research tissue bank. Quotient's human tissue bank is the foundation of our proprietary high-resolution somatic genetics platform, which delivers insights into cellular and organ disease biology and discovers novel targets for the development of new medicines.

You will lead across the whole sample lifecycle, from procurement review and receipt through storage, use, reuse, transfer and disposal, and keep Quotient compliant with its Human Tissue Authority (HTA) research licence.

Reporting to the Head of Research Strategy and Operations, you will work closely with the Director of Partnerships to check that proposed research fits the permissions and restrictions attached to each collection. You will also be the central point of coordination between laboratory teams, Facilities, Procurement and Logistics, Project Leads and Data Infrastructure, so that colleagues get timely access to suitable samples with full end-to-end traceability.

This role combines ownership of the tissue bank with practical oversight of delivery. Success means reliable, well-organised inventory and chain-of-custody records, timely availability of samples for research, compliance with internal SOPs and HTA regulations, and effective resolution of any sample-related incidents.

Key responsibilities

  • Biobank governance and strategy: Own Quotient's research tissue bank strategy, aligning governance, capacity, resources and operating systems with the research portfolio, and recommend investment and improvements. Report sample availability, integrity, traceability, compliance risks and incident trends to leadership.
  • HTA compliance: Act as the HTA Designated Individual for Quotient's research licence, supervising licensed activities and making sure that staff, premises, storage and procedures meet HTA requirements. Develop SOPs, oversee training and competency assurance, and lead inspection readiness and responses, covering UK HTA, GDPR, research ethics and health and safety standards.
  • Sample access and use authorisation: Review access, initial use, reuse and onward transfer against consent, research ethics approvals, licence scope and contractual permissions, and document each decision. Apply independent judgement to complex sample-use decisions, balancing scientific priorities with donor permissions, sample availability and governance requirements, and obtain specialist advice or further approvals where needed.
  • Sample acquisition and custody: Own custody controls from handover at receipt through registration, storage, retrieval, distribution and disposal, including manifests, shipment conditions, acceptance checks, handovers and receipt acknowledgements. Set requirements for human tissue shipments and approve the release of inbound and outbound shipments, working with logistics colleagues who handle couriers and documentation. Provide cover for sample receipt and shipping, directly or through trained delegates.
  • Inventory systems and traceability: Integrate sample inventory with LIMS and ELN records, keeping identifiers, parent–derivative relationships, quantities, locations, status and movement histories accurate through timely updates, controlled access and periodic reconciliation. Ensure accurate annotation and metadata for all biospecimens, work with the Data Infrastructure team to bring sample data into research pipelines, and report on utilisation, inventory status and operational metrics.
  • Storage integrity and continuity: Manage storage organisation and capacity with laboratory and facilities colleagues. Work with the team that owns the temperature-monitoring system to make sure it is fit for purpose and supports HTA compliance, sign off monitoring procedures and the training of staff who use it, and check calibration and alarm-test records as part of routine internal audits. Own specimen decisions during alarms and recovery, including integrity assessment, transfers, holds and incident recording, and agree documented default actions so that out-of-hours response does not wait for a specimen decision.
  • Incident resolution and corrective action: Escalate concerns, pause non-compliant activities and hold samples where eligibility, documentation or integrity is unresolved. Run a quality-driven incident process, track corrective and preventive actions and approve closure.
  • Capability and culture: Build capability through coaching, knowledge sharing and effective cover arrangements across the biobank and sample-management network. Create an environment where colleagues raise concerns, learn from incidents and share accountability.

About you

You are an experienced biobanking or human tissue governance leader who combines sound regulatory judgement with practical delivery. You can make and explain proportionate decisions, influence across functions and build quality-based systems that support a growing research portfolio.

Essential criteria

  • BSc in Biological Sciences, Biomedical Sciences or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • More than 5 years working with human biological samples in a research, biotechnology, biobank or clinical laboratory setting, including leadership of sample governance and operations across the sample lifecycle.
  • Demonstrated leadership, including setting direction, developing colleagues and capability, influencing senior stakeholders without direct authority, and resolving competing priorities.
  • Experience working across a variety of quality systems, and able to interpret guidelines and apply basic principles in a research setting.
  • Experience reviewing consent, ethics and provenance documentation, interpreting sample-use restrictions, and assessing proposed use, reuse and transfer in collaboration with scientific, partnerships and legal colleagues.
  • Experience reviewing sample-related provisions in MTAs, SLAs, MSAs or equivalent agreements and translating those obligations into operational controls.
  • Proven ownership of sample accessioning, chain of custody, storage, database inventory and distribution processes, with practical experience of LIMS, ELN or comparable systems and their data quality and access controls.
  • Strong working knowledge of the Human Tissue Act 2004, HTA research licensing and relevant standards, with experience supporting or leading licensed activities.
  • Experience developing controlled documentation, training staff, preparing for audits or inspections, and leading incident investigations, corrective and preventive actions and documented closure.
  • Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and professional judgement, with a commitment to donor respect, confidentiality, scientific quality and continuous improvement.

Desirable criteria

  • Previous appointment as an HTA Designated Individual, or substantial experience as a Person Designated with responsibility for tissue governance, inspections and compliance improvement.
  • Familiarity with handling low-complexity clinical data and associated regulatory frameworks (GDPR).
  • Experience in genomics, molecular biology or high-throughput research, including support for histology, flow cytometry or molecular workflows.
  • Experience with cryogenic storage, freezer monitoring, sample integrity assessment and business continuity arrangements.
  • Knowledge or experience of REC applications.
  • Experience coordinating domestic and international sample transfers, external biobanks, offsite sample storage companies or CROs, and working with third-party logistics teams within a growing biotechnology organisation.
  • Experience developing colleagues or leading a biobank or sample reception team, and implementing inventory platforms or significant process improvements.
  • Evidence of building or improving tissue bank processes and systems, planning capacity and resources, and balancing scientific delivery with ethical and regulatory responsibilities.

About Quotient:

Quotient Therapeutics is a privately-held, early stage company developing breakthrough medicines informed by natural somatic genetic diversity present in patients. Through our work in somatic genomics, we are forging a new status quo for biopharma research and development across a broad pipeline of internal and partnered programs. 

The company was founded by Flagship Pioneering, an innovative enterprise that conceives, creates, resources, and grows first-in-category life sciences companies. Flagship Pioneering has created over 100 groundbreaking companies over the past twenty years, all of which are pioneering novel and proprietary biological, industrial, and engineering approaches to solve major needs in human health and sustainability. These companies include Moderna (MRNA), Generate Biomedicines, Sana Biotechnology (SANA), Tessera Therapeutics, Evelo Biosciences (EVLO), Indigo Agriculture, Seres Therapeutics (MCRB), and Syros Pharmaceuticals (SYRS).

Quotient Therapeutics and Flagship Pioneering are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

Recruitment & Staffing Agencies:

Quotient Therapeutics (“Quotient”) and Flagship Pioneering (“FSP”) do not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to Quotient, FSP or their employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Flagship Pioneering’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of FSP, and FSP will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

Privacy Notice for Applicants: When you apply for a role at Flagship Pioneering or one of its portfolio companies, we collect and use personal information you provide (such as your name, contact details, work history, and application materials) to evaluate your application, communicate with you, and comply with legal obligations. Your application data is processed through Greenhouse, our applicant tracking system, and may also be reviewed using AI-assisted screening tools. We do not sell your personal information. California residents have rights under the CCPA/CPRA including to know, delete, and opt out of the sharing of their personal information. If you are located in the EU or UK, we process your data under GDPR and you have rights to access, rectify, and erase your data. To exercise your rights or for questions, contact -----

title: Build Your Own Role – m/f/d
descriptionHtml:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe’s largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

 

About the Role

This is not a regular open application. We don’t want your CV first. We want to see what you have built.

You may build with AI because you can’t stop, whether that’s with Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or whatever gets the job done. You may also know you’d add real value at Langdock without seeing the right opening on our careers page. If both are true, this is your door.

Show us a project. If it convinces us, we build the role around you.

 

What We Want to See

Record a Loom of something you built with AI. It should be no longer than 5 minutes. Two kinds of projects get our attention:

  • Something that would help Langdock. Look at our product roadmap and at our product, and build something that solves a real problem for us or our customers. That could be a feature prototype, an internal tool, a GTM engine, a support automation, an eval setup, or something we haven’t thought of yet.

  • A genuine passion project. Something you built because you couldn’t stop thinking about it, and that shows how you think.

What we don’t want: basic chatbots, simple prompt wrappers, “summarize my inbox” agents, or linear three-step workflows. Our customers build those every day. Show us something that made you think hard, and that makes us think too.

 

What Your Loom Should Cover

  • The problem: what you solved and why it matters.

  • The demo: show it working live, not on slides.

  • How it’s built: the models, tools, architecture, and key decisions behind it.

  • What broke: where it failed and what you learned from that.

  • What’s next: what you would build at Langdock if you joined.

 

How to Apply

Paste your Loom link into the field “Your Build” in the application form. Your LinkedIn profile is enough; a CV is optional.

 

What Happens Next

We watch every Loom. If your build stands out, we invite you to go deep on your project with us. Together we then define where you would have the most impact. That could be Product, Engineering, GTM, Customer Success, Operations, or a role that doesn’t exist yet.

 

You Might Be a Fit If…

  • You build, not just talk about AI. You have shipped things that work, even if they’re rough.

  • You think in impact. You care about whether something solves a real problem for real users, not just whether it is technically clever.

  • You show high agency and full ownership. Nobody needs to tell you what to do next.

  • You experiment constantly. You try new models, tools, and approaches as soon as they come out.

  • You communicate clearly and professionally in English. German is a plus.

  • You are kind and care about the people around you.

 

What We Need

  • Availability to work full-time and 100% on-site at our Berlin office.

  • A work permit for Germany.

 

The Environment

You will work from our Berlin office at Greifswalder Straße 212, where all of us work together in person, surrounded by people building AI products and infrastructure every day. Lunch and dinner are catered in the office. We look after ourselves, and gym membership and coaching resources are part of the standard package. We value Calm Urgency, Ambitious Execution, and Caring Ownership. The vibe is calm but intense.

 

Compensation

Salaries are transparent and tied to levels, not negotiation. We define the level together once the role is clear.

About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

title: CDI - Senior AI Engineer - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Mission

De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.
  • Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.
  • Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.
  • Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.
  • Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.
  • Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.
  • Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.
  2. Votre code est testé et maintenable.
  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
  4. La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.
  5. Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.
  6. Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.
  • Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.
  • Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.
  • Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.
  • Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en production, bases de la sécurité de l’IA).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.
  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).
  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.
  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.
  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.
  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 60 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) selon expérience et séniorité + jusqu’à 6 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

title: CDI - Senior AI Strategist - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Prenez en main un stream de transformation IA, au contact direct des clients, de la vision aux résultats mesurables.

L’IA, et en particulier l’IA agentique, figure parmi les priorités des comités de direction.
Chez Artefact, nous sommes des makers. “We Make AI Work” : notre métier n’est pas de commenter l’IA, c’est de la faire fonctionner, à grande échelle, au cœur des grands groupes. 

Et tout commence par vous.

Mission

En tant que Senior AI Strategist, vous prenez en main un stream ou une mission bien cadrée, avec autonomie sur votre périmètre et au contact direct des clients : vous cadrez, analysez, prototypez et recommandez, vous coachez les consultants juniors, et vous voyez vos recommandations prendre vie avec nos équipes Engineering.

Vous commencez là où débute toute transformation IA : par l’ambition du client, son secteur d’activité et ses processus métier, et non par la technologie. Et vous restez un maker : vous ne vous arrêtez pas au slide. Vous construisez vous-même analyses, business cases et démos fonctionnelles (vibe coding, low-code, no-code) que le client peut toucher, et vous développez un domaine d’expertise solide dans un secteur ou une fonction métier.

Vous travaillez main dans la main avec nos équipes Engineering (qui construisent et livrent des solutions d’IA agentique) et nos équipes AI Adoption (qui favorisent leur adoption) : vous cadrez les processus cibles et la roadmap de votre stream, Engineering les construit et les livre, et AI Adoption accompagne les personnes dans le changement, dès le premier jour.


Activités & Responsabilités

  • Conception de la stratégie et de la transformation IA

Vous contribuez à cadrer la vision IA et à la roadmap du stream, qualifiez et priorisez les cas d’usage, et arbitrez entre solutions IA et non-IA. Vous investiguez les processus métier, identifiez les irritants et les causes racines, et proposez des pistes de refonte priorisées, en pensant d’abord lean et en n’utilisant l’IA que là où elle apporte de la valeur. Vous contribuez également à la conception du modèle opératoire cible et à ses conditions de succès.

  • Analyses, business cases & prototypage

Vous concevez et pilotez les travaux d’analyse du stream afin de sécuriser des décisions fondées sur les données et sur les faits : vous collectez et validez les données, revoyez les analyses des consultants juniors, construisez des business cases de bout en bout et formulez des recommandations. Vous prototypez des cas d’usage avec des outils agentiques pour illustrer la valeur par la démo et aider les clients à se projeter dans la solution finale.

  • Delivery, livrables & collaboration

Vous pilotez au quotidien la livraison d’un stream ou d’une mission cadrée : vous construisez le rétro-planning, identifiez les risques et blocages, proposez des solutions et donnez de la visibilité au N+1 et aux équipes du client. Vous produisez des sections de livrables de niveau C-suite, rédigez les storylines du stream, participez aux synthèses exécutives sur votre périmètre et construisez un narratif qui appuie la recommandation et emporte l’adhésion. Vous coordonnez votre stream avec les équipes Engineering pour la faisabilité technique et avec les équipes AI Adoption pour ancrer l’adoption sur le terrain.

  • Relation client & développement commercial

Vous construisez une relation de proximité avec votre interlocuteur direct, élargissez le réseau de parties prenantes aux équipes opérationnelles et au middle management, anticipez les résistances et animez des ateliers en autonomie. Vous identifiez des opportunités, soutenez le plan de compte avec le Manager et le Directeur et participez aux propositions et aux événements de networking.

  • Équipe & connaissances

Vous déléguez avec des instructions claires, donnez des feedbacks constructifs, animez des 1to1 avec les consultants juniors et participez aux rétrospectives et aux entretiens de candidats. Vous contribuez à la base de connaissances interne par des articles et des retours d’expérience, et animez des sessions d’onboarding et des formations internes.

Profil recherché

Vous vous reconnaissez si… vous aimez avoir la main sur un périmètre, structurer des problèmes complexes et voir vos recommandations se concrétiser, et si vous préférez mettre une démo entre les mains du client plutôt que lui décrire une vision.

  • 2 à 5 ans d’expérience au sein d’un cabinet de conseil en stratégie, en management ou en transformation data / IA.

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
descriptionHtml:
The question

Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards.

What you will do

The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request.

1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report.

2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured.

3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along.

4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements.

A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.


Who we are looking for Required

• A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract.

• A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models.

• Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure.

• Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI.

• Working English; French is not required.

Valued, not required

Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.

What matters most

We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.

What we offer

• A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot.

• A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design.

• Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI).

• Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers.

• Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling.

Conditions

Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment.

title: Chief Engineer, Maritime
descriptionHtml:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

UFORCE is looking for a Chief Engineer to take end-to-end technical ownership of a priority product family, platform, or cross-product mission system spanning air, land, maritime, payloads, and enabling technologies.

Our systems have been shaped by extensive real-world operational use. The next challenge is to turn that advantage into globally deployable products that continuously improve, move rapidly from operator need to fielded capability, and can be produced reliably at scale.

You will be the accountable technical leader for the complete system: translating mission needs into requirements, leading architecture and design decisions across disciplines, driving performance improvements, and ensuring that products are integrated, testable, manufacturable, reliable, and ready for operational use. You will work closely with UFORCE's technical founder, Hardware and Software leadership, Product, Manufacturing, Delivery, and engineering teams across Ukraine and Global markets.

This is not a role for someone who wants to manage engineering from a distance. You will remain close to the technology, the people building it, and the operators using it - leading design reviews, supporting tests and deployments, resolving difficult system-level problems, and creating the technical clarity that allows strong engineers to move quickly.

The role is ideally based in the United Kingdom and will require regular travel to UFORCE engineering, manufacturing, test, and deployment locations.

What you'll do

  • Take end-to-end technical ownership of an assigned UFORCE product family, platform, or integrated mission system.

  • Translate operator needs, customer requirements, field evidence, and strategic priorities into clear system requirements, architecture, interfaces, and acceptance criteria.

  • Lead technical trade-offs across mechanical, electrical, electronics, controls, embedded software, autonomy, communications, payloads, power, manufacturing, and operational constraints.

  • Identify and deliver material improvements to mission performance, including areas such as range, endurance, payload, accuracy, survivability, speed, reliability, and operator effectiveness.

  • Accelerate the path from mission need to tested and fielded capability through rapid, evidence-led build-test-learn cycles.

  • Establish and maintain a coherent technical baseline across requirements, system architecture, interfaces, configurations, and regional product variants.

  • Ensure designs are manufacturable, testable, maintainable, supportable, and capable of being produced repeatedly at the required rate and quality.

  • Use test, deployment, exercise, operator, and combat evidence to diagnose failures, establish root causes, and drive verified corrective action.

  • Lead high-quality requirements, architecture, design, integration, test-readiness, and release-readiness reviews without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Build and develop a lean, high-performing cross-disciplinary engineering team with clear ownership, strong technical standards, and a low-ego approach to problem-solving.

  • Partner closely with Software Engineering and Pavel's organization to ensure hardware, software, controls, compute, and autonomy operate as one integrated system.

  • Personally intervene when a priority technical issue or programme is blocked and remain accountable until the system-level problem is resolved.

What we're looking for

  • Significant experience as a Chief Engineer, Chief Systems Engineer, Technical Director, Head of Engineering, Chief Designer, Engineering Director, or equivalent senior technical authority for a complex physical system.

  • Evidence of having owned a product or system through requirements, architecture, design, integration, verification, production release, and real-world operation.

  • Broad systems judgment across multiple engineering disciplines, with the ability to understand interactions, challenge assumptions, and lead consequential technical trade-offs.

  • A track record of materially improving system or product performance using first-principles engineering, structured experimentation, and objective evidence.

  • Experience shortening development or upgrade cycles in a high-consequence environment while maintaining appropriate safety, design assurance, configuration control, and verification.

  • Experience taking a complex product from prototype or low-volume development into repeatable production, or materially improving reliability, quality, yield, maintainability, cost, or throughput.

  • The technical credibility to lead highly capable specialists without needing to be the deepest expert in every discipline.

  • A leadership style that develops engineers, creates clear ownership, encourages constructive challenge, and treats failed hypotheses as a source of learning rather than blame.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, globally distributed environment with incomplete structure, constrained resources, and rapidly changing priorities.

  • Willingness to work directly with engineers, factories, test teams, deployed personnel, customers, and operators wherever the most important technical problem exists.

Nice to have

  • Experience developing unmanned, autonomous, robotic, aerospace, maritime, defense, or other safety- or mission-critical systems.

  • Direct experience supporting military customers, live exercises, demonstrations, deployments, or operationally fielded products.

  • Experience in an engineering environment characterized by rapid iteration, tight performance margins, and demanding delivery cycles.

  • Familiarity with integrated hardware-software systems, embedded controls, autonomy, communications, payload integration, or system-of-systems architecture.

  • Experience adapting a common product architecture across countries, regulatory environments, supply chains, or customer-specific configurations.

  • Experience building or turning around an engineering team, function, or technical operating model in a startup or high-growth environment.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

Are You?

title: Closer (m/f) - Investor Relations in Düsseldorf
descriptionHtml:
Late shift. High stakes. Six US time zones. One shot per call.

This is a genuine job posting - not a ghost job!

Let's skip the part where we tell you this is “an exciting opportunity in a dynamic environment.” You've read that sentence four hundred times and seen it all.

Here's what's actually true:

We need an experienced, financially literate Closer who speaks English on a native or C2 Level, can pick up a phone at 3:30pm, talk to a stranger with eight figures in a brokerage account somewhere in Wyoming or Connecticut, get them to sign a convertible promissory note before their assistant walks in with coffee. That's it. That's the job. Everything else is detail.

Who We Are

Meridion AG runs the show from Monheim & Düsseldorf. Our US arm, Meridion Dynamics Inc., builds intelligent software and smart energy technology. But you're not selling the product. You're closing the investment that funds it. Different animal, different muscle.

Aufgaben

What You'll Actually Do

  • Take warm(ish) leads from our setters - accredited US investors who already know we called - and close them on convertible promissory notes.
  • Walk investors through the accreditation process without losing them to paperwork fatigue.
  • Hold the line, know the terms cold, and answer the “wait, what happens if you don't hit your IPO timeline” question without blinking.
  • If a setter is running low on appointments, out sick or on vacation, you step in and run up to 100 outbound cold calls that day to convert cold leads into your Closing appointments. Yes, a hundred. We count :)
  • Talk to people who have people and AI to screen their calls - and get past their Gatekeepers.

Qualifikation

What You Bring

  • Real closing experience - several years of it, in high-ticket sales, investment products, or anything else where “no” is the opening bid, not the final answer. This is not a rookie position.
  • English at a genuine native level. Not “I watched a lot of Suits.” You need to sound like you belong in a room with a family office CFO. If it's not your first language, we're talking true C2, no exceptions. An accent is no Dealbreaker but your vocabulary, your pronunciation, the way you use idioms - your vibe on the phone - must be on fleek.
  • A voice and presence that reads as calm, unbothered, and confident - think less “modern hustle culture” - more Brian Tracy.
  • Genuine understanding of what an accredited investor is, what a convertible note does, and why someone would put $50k+ into one. We'll brief you thoroughly - but you need financial literacy to keep up from day one.
  • A working understanding of US investor culture, even sitting in Düsseldorf’s Seestern District.

Benefits

The Deal

  • Full-time, 40h/week, onsite at our Düsseldorf office near Seestern.
  • Late shift: 2:30pm - 10pm, because your workday runs on Pacific and Eastern time, not Berlin time.
  • Base salary + commission
  • Onboarding is real: Expect a genuine ramp-up before you're fully solo on calls.
  • Start: ASAP - which translates to “realistically September/October”.

Not For You If

You cling to a script forever to feel confident. You've never been told “no” 70 times in a day and called it Tuesday. You think “Closer” means you show up after someone else already did the hard part.

Sound like your Tuesday? Send us your CV.
We don’t do 5 interview rounds.
You talk to me on the phone or in a brief Teams Video Call.

If I sense you’re a fit, we’ll welcome you onsite for another brief interview with our CEO; please plan in approximately 2h for the interview, a brief vibe check with the team and one or two test calls so we can hear your closing performance.

That’s it.

title: Cloud Architect (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Wir sind Royal Runtimes. Wir bauen AI-Systeme, bevor andere darüber Folien machen.

Wir sind ein kleines AI-Studio in Hamburg. Wir beraten Unternehmen zu AI und bauen dabei genau die Dinge, die wir selbst jeden Tag benutzen. Manche davon werden zu eigenen Produkten, die wir mit Partnern als Joint Ventures launchen. Andere bauen wir nur für uns, weil wir sie brauchen.

Eines dieser Ventures ist eine PaaS für Builder Companies auf Google Cloud: eine Plattform, auf der Unternehmen ihre eigene Software mit AI bauen und betreiben. Für ihre Architektur suchen wir jemanden, der Google Cloud besser kennt als wir beide zusammen.

Mit wem du arbeitest

Henning hat bei Tchibo als Head of AI Engineering & Platform die AI-Transformation vorangetrieben. Mit GPT-1 hat er schon unlustige Witze-Bots gebaut, als noch niemand Sprachmodelle kannte. Als studierter Statistiker hat er sogar manchmal Ahnung, wovon er redet.

Erik hat Consulting einmal komplett durchgespielt, zuletzt als Business Unit Manager Data & AI bei Reply. Im früheren Leben war er Data Scientist, Python-Enthusiast, ML-Evangelist, Contributor bei Apache Spark und MLflow, blahblahblah.

Du gehörst zu unseren ersten Einstellungen und arbeitest vom ersten Tag an direkt mit uns beiden. Wir werden kontinuierlich wachsen. Du lernst viel von uns, und wir wollen auch von dir lernen: die neue Harness, die du am Wochenende getestet hast, den neuen Skill, der unsere CI/CD 100x besser macht.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass wir unsere AI-PaaS auf Hunderte Enterprise-Kunden skalieren und betreiben können.
  • Du steuerst Agents. Die Guidelines und die Governance, nach denen sie Terraform, Pipelines und Code bauen, entwickelst du selbst. So skalieren wir unsere Software Factory.
  • Wir treffen die technischen Grundsatzentscheidungen der Plattform gemeinsam, unter deiner Führung.
  • Du arbeitest am Produkt. In Beratungsprojekte holen wir dich für Strategiefragen oder wenn ein Team nicht weiterkommt.

Was du mitbringst

  • Mindestens 6 Jahre Erfahrung mit Google Cloud. Du hast dort Plattformen entworfen, gebaut und in Produktion betrieben.
  • Du bist die Person, die gefragt wird, wenn bei Google Cloud sonst niemand weiterweiß.
  • Du könntest jede Ressource selbst in Terraform schreiben. Du lässt das Agenten machen und bist das Mastermind hinter deiner Agent Fleet.
  • AI ist dein Beruf und dein Hobby. Wenn im AI-Umfeld etwas Neues erscheint, hast du es ausprobiert, bevor andere davon gelesen haben. Egal ob Modell, Tool, Framework oder Hardware.
  • Du baust lieber, als darüber zu reden.
  • Du willst jeden Tag dazulernen und kannst mit Feedback umgehen.
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch.

Was dich erwartet

  • Keine Limits beim Werkzeug. Tokens, Hardware, Software: Du bekommst, was du für sehr gute Arbeit brauchst. Wir sehen das als Arbeitsmittel und diskutieren nicht über Budgets.
  • Ein Venture, das du mit aufbaust. Die PaaS ist ein eigenes Produkt neben unserem Kundengeschäft. Du bist früh dabei und übernimmst dort eine entscheidende Rolle.
  • Kunden mit Anspruch. Konzerne und große Mittelständler, die wirklich umbauen wollen, Private-Equity-Portfolios und Startups. Was wir in diesen Projekten über Builder Companies lernen, fließt in die Plattform.
  • Büro in der HafenCity. Wir arbeiten jeden Tag zusammen vor Ort, mit Blick über die ganze Stadt.

Das passt nicht, wenn

  • du lieber allein im Homeoffice sitzt, als mit uns zusammen zu bauen.
  • du klare Prozesse und ein fertiges Ticket-Board erwartest.
  • du Terraform lieber selbst tippst, als es Agenten schreiben zu lassen.
  • du AI für einen Hype hältst.

So bewirbst du dich

Kein Anschreiben. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und erklär uns deine Vision dafür, wie man state-of-the-art Enterprise-Cloud-Architekturen vollständig durch Agents aufbauen und betreiben kann.

So geht's weiter

title: Compliance Director
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Compliance Director and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

  • Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

  • Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

  • Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

  • Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

  • Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

  • Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

  • CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

  • People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

Wir sind eine junge Beratung mit Fokus auf Strategie, Technologie und Umsetzung. Wir arbeiten für große Unternehmen an anspruchsvollen Projekten, insbesondere in den Bereichen Energiewirtschaft, Netzintegration und Data Center.

title: Control & Estimation Intern
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

We are developing the flight control systems of our next-generation autonomous platforms, which are embedded and subjected to extreme operational constraints. As with any aeronautical system, no model is perfect: aerodynamic effects, actuator dynamics, wind, payload changes, damage or degraded sensors are never fully captured by the physics-based models we rely on.

These unmodelled dynamics are one of the main sources of performance loss and risk for a controller, especially at the edge of the flight envelope. To push the boundaries of control, we are working on estimating these disturbances online and compensating for them in real time through adaptive control and robust estimation.

Your mission

The goal of this internship is to design, implement and validate a framework for estimating and compensating unmodelled physics disturbances, in order to improve the robustness and performance of our flight controller in extreme and uncertain conditions.

Responsibilities

  • Literature review: Survey existing approaches to disturbance estimation and adaptive control

  • Algorithm implementation: Develop and implement the selected estimation and compensation algorithms within our simulation environment.

  • Performance evaluation: Assess and compare the performance and robustness of the developed methods against classical baselines.

  • Embedded constraints: Ensure the solutions are compatible with real-time execution and the computational limits of onboard hardware.

  • Documentation: Document all work performed, including methodologies, results and conclusions.

  • Flight test participation: Actively take part in flight test sessions to validate the developed algorithms in operational conditions, and contribute to their real-time deployment.

Candidates Requirements

  • Educational background: Strong academic record in automatic control, applied mathematics, or a related field. Knowledge of state estimation (Kalman filtering, observers) and nonlinear or adaptive control is a strong plus.

  • Technical skills: Solid understanding of control theory fundamentals and proficiency in Python or C++ is a plus. Experience with drones is a major plus.

  • Mindset: You are curious to learn, autonomous, rigorous and able to take initiative.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Customer Success Account Manager, Mid-Market
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

You help customers adopt the platform, realise measurable value, and renew and expand with confidence. You pick up where Implementation leaves off, learn each customer's fleet and challenges, and advise on tailoring Samsara to them. You manage 100+ named accounts, using AI tooling to extend your reach and focus your time where it counts. Your understanding of the value customers get earns you the right to lead the ROI conversation, negotiate terms and close renewals that work for both sides, minimising financial attrition. You work with Sales, Support, Deal Desk, Operations and Product.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. This team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

  • Deeply understand the Samsara platform's capabilities and explain them to businesses of all types, from field services and utilities to long-haul transportation and school buses.
  • Manage a portfolio of 100+ named accounts, using AI tooling to accelerate your engagement, prioritize proactively, and drive efficiency and outcomes across your book of business.
  • Lead the ROI and value conversation into the renewal, negotiate favorable terms, and close renewals that are a win for both the customer and Samsara while minimizing financial attrition.
  • Demonstrate a willingness to understand and explain technical issues to a non-technical audience and to engage the right cross-functional partners to drive resolution.
  • Conduct workshops with customers to understand their current operations and recommend workflow changes to maximize the value of their Samsara products.
  • Work cross-functionally with Sales, Support, Deal Desk, Operations and Product to strategically solve problems and optimize customer experience and business outcomes.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Business fluency in French (spoken and written).
  • 2+ years in a customer-facing, quota-carrying role (renewals, customer success, account management or sales), ideally in SaaS, technology or logistics.
  • A record of consistent quota over-achievement.
  • Strong problem-solving, communication and presentation skills, and the ability to build trust with executives, users and internal teams.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Gainsight, Gong or similar GTM tools.
  • Comfort in a fast-changing, high-growth environment.
  • A bachelor's degree from a 4-year institution, or equivalent practical experience.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • A strong bias towards action, big-picture thinking and high standards.
  • An AI-first approach: you use AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
  • Technical depth across a suite of products, with a bonus for hardware-software integration.
  • Industry Knowledge: Experience with routing, navigation, commercial trucking fleets, and logistics.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in ----- ----- or ----- For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

title: Customer Success Manager (KI-Fokus) - m/w/d
descriptionHtml:
Was wir suchen

Eine Person, die ihre Freunde als „technisch-affinen Menschenfreund“ beschreiben würden, und Lust darauf hat zu erklären und zu beraten.

Aufgaben

  1. Kickoff: Du führst Kickoff-Calls per Video mit neuen Kunden und klärst, wie die Prozesse, die wir für sie automatisieren aussehen.

  2. Setup: Du richtest KI-Systeme nach unserem festen, dokumentierten Standard ein und verbindest ihn mit den Plattformen des Kunden, zum Beispiel Mail, Kalender und etc.

  3. Onboarding: Du begleitest den Kunden, bis alles rund läuft – mit Onboarding-Call und einer Woche Feedback-Runde.

  4. Support: Du betreust unsere bestehenden Kunden und antwortest innerhalb von 24 Stunden. Einen Großteil der Anfragen erledigt unsere KI, du kümmerst dich um den Rest.

  5. Kundenbeziehung: Du schreibst mit den Kunden, beantwortest Fragen und sorgst dafür, dass sie zufrieden sind 🤝

  6. Produkt: Du sammelst Fehler und Kundenfeedback und gehst sie einmal pro Woche mit unserem Team durch, und wirkst aktiv an der Verbesserung unserer Produkte mit.

  7. Tempo: Nach der Einarbeitung betreust du mehrere Setups parallel und startest bis zu einen neuen Kunden pro Tag.

So arbeiten wir dich ein

  1. Woche 1: Du lernst unsere Abläufe, unser Studio und den Setup-Standard kennen und baust deinen eigenen KI-Agenten, falls du noch keinen hast (inkl. aller relevanten Schulungen).

  2. Woche 2: Du bist bei Kickoff-Calls und Setups unseres Technik-Teams dabei.

  3. Ab Woche 3: Du führst deinen ersten eigenen Kickoff, und hast einen Mentor an deiner Seite, der dich dabei unterstützt.

  4. Nach rund 4 Wochen: Du machst Calls, Setup und Support eigenständig und übernimmst nach und nach immer mehr Eigenverantwortung.

Qualifikation

  • Du magst Technik und Menschen gleichermaßen und hast ggf. selbst mit KI-Werkzeugen wie Claude Code, Codex oder eigenen Agenten gearbeitet.

  • Du telefonierst gern und erklärst Technik so, dass dich ein Schreinermeister und ein Geschäftsführer gleichermaßen verstehen.

  • Du arbeitest sorgfältig und verantwortungsbewusst, gerade mit Kundendaten.

  • Du willst Gas geben, dazulernen und persönlich wachsen.

  • Deutsch fließend in Wort und Schrift (C2), denn unsere Kunden sind deutsche Unternehmer. Englisch hilft bei Dokumentation und Tools, ist aber keine Bedingung.

  • Optional: Du wohnst im Umkreis von Düsseldorf oder München (unsere Standorte)

  • Welcher Abschluss dahintersteht, ist uns egal. Unsere Abläufe sind dokumentiert und lernbar – du musst nicht alles von Anfang an können.

Wer nicht zu uns passt:

  • Jemand, der lieber nur am Code sitzt und Kundengespräche als Störung empfindet.

  • Jemand, der Dienst nach Vorschrift sucht. Wir erwarten keine Dauerbereitschaft und kein Wochenende am Laptop, aber dass du Dinge zu Ende denkst und einen eigenen Anspruch an die Exzellenz deiner Arbeit hast ⭐

Wie geht's weiter?

Kein Lebenslauf, kein 0815-Anschreiben. Beantworte ein paar kurze Fragen und beantworte in deinem Anschreiben in eigenen Worten (*nicht KI-geschrieben*):

1) Was hast du bisher selbst mit KI gebaut?

2) Welche KI-Themen interessieren dich aktuell am meisten als Lernfeld?

3) Warum könntest du der perfekte Fit für diese Rolle sein?

title: Customer Success Manager, Upmarket - EMEA
descriptionHtml:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust.We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 

As Vanta’s Customer Success Manager in the Upmarket space (Enterprise/Mid-Market), you will play a pivotal role in guiding customers through their security and compliance journeys with Vanta's specialised solutions. By combining your customer-centric approach with expertise in Vanta's products and security best practices, you will contribute to the overall success and satisfaction of Vanta's customers in achieving robust security and compliance outcomes through retention of customers and health of the book of business.

Vanta’s success over the last year was exponential, and we are now working to solve the problem of how to provide world-class customer experience to as many security-minded software companies as possible. As Vanta’s Customer Success Manager, you will be the voice of Vanta, responsible for helping keep our customers moving toward their goals and ultimately successful and happy.

What you’ll do as a Customer Success Manager in the Upmarket segment at Vanta:

  • Lead all post-sales activities for Vanta’s customers through onboarding, implementation, product expertise, renewal and identifying upsell opportunities.

  • Partner with Account Managers to drive renewal and expansion opportunities within your book of business.

  • Act as the voice of the customer within Vanta.

  • Serve as the point of contact for your customers and drive them to specific business outcomes on their timelines.

  • Become a product expert on Vanta and how our platform can be used to improve security posture through our compliance offerings (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, USDP and Custom Frameworks), Trust Reports, and Risk Management solution.

  • Provide insightful technical answers and recommend the most efficient way for customers to achieve compliance using our platform.

  • Develop a trusted advisor relationship with key accounts, customer stakeholders, and executive sponsors that may lead to renewals, expansion, and advocacy.

  • Influence Vanta’s strategy and product priorities to drive adoption and retention by being the voice of the customer.

  • Work cross-functionally to resolve customer business issues and work toward mutual goals.

How to be successful in this role:

  • Have 6+ years of experience in Customer Success at a SaaS company.

  • Extensive experience with high-end exposure to C-level executives, and the ability to build strong trusted relationships.

  • Providing top-notch account management and relationship building through various means; Quarterly Business Reviews, Health Check Ins, and Executive summaries etc

  • Ability to be nimble and agile in an environment where shifting priorities should be expected.

  • Experience working in the security or compliance industry is preferred.

  • Possess clear and thoughtful communication skills, with strong critical thinking ability.

  • Be highly empathetic to customers, with a proven track record of long-term customer retention.

  • Experience with hitting retention targets and creating happy, healthy customers.

  • Possess the technical competency to understand Vanta’s software and build great relationships with highly technical customers.

  • Have stellar problem-solving chops, and an enthusiasm for making a large impact early on at a start-up.

  • Uses AI in day-to-day work to amplify their skills and strengthen their outcomes, applying it across routine workflows, actively building fluency through experimentation, and exercising sound judgment to ensure AI-assisted work meets a high quality bar.

What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

  • Industry-competitive salary and equity

  • 100% covered medical, dental, and vision benefits with dependents coverage

  • 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents Health & wellness stipend

  • Remote workspace, internet, and mobile phone stipend

  • Commuter benefits for team members who attend the office

    • FYI we are in the office Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays

  • Pension matching

  • 25 days of Annual Leave per year and unlimited sick time

  • 8 company-paid holidays

  • Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

  • Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

#LI-hybrid

At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.

About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.
